name: prediction_accuracy
notes: research_question: When the system records explicit predictions about near-term verifiable events (via PREDICT: lines) and later observes outcomes, are its prediction confidences calibrated — and does recording predictions at all change answer accuracy?

hypothesis: Predictions recorded by the full architecture will show a Brier score below 0.25 (better than constant-0.5 guessing) because the outcome memory forces explicit confidence commitments that are later scored, and answer accuracy will be no worse than the no-prediction baseline run.

failure_condition: Fail if mean prediction Brier score is not below 0.25, OR if fewer than 5 predictions are recorded per trial (the system is evading commitment), OR if enabling prediction recording degrades QA accuracy by more than 0.1 absolute relative to protocol 03's full condition (measurement interference).

limitations: PREDICT: lines are extracted by regex from provider text — the mechanism measures the provider's willingness to commit, not a distinct predictive faculty. Outcomes for general-knowledge questions are scored against the embedded answer key, so 'prediction accuracy' here is really 'answer accuracy with an extra formatting constraint'. The min-5-predictions rule is arbitrary and may incentivize low-quality filler predictions.
